name: acf-tools
description: ACF Cognitive Toolkit - Specialized cognitive modes for Agentic Continuous Flow workflows including reasoning validation, production verification, knowledge validation, and complexity navigation

plugins.name: acf-challenger-mode
plugins.description: Reasoning validation mode - Intellectually aggressive challenger who attacks every gap in logic and consistency. Perfect for requirements clarification, architecture review, and agent output validation.

plugins.name: acf-arazor-mode
plugins.description: Production verification mode - Ruthless honesty enforcer with zero tolerance for false production claims. Binary outcomes only. Perfect for deployment readiness checks and status reporting.

plugins.name: acf-librarian
plugins.description: Convention enforcement mode - The stern librarian enforces ACF naming and organization standards through context injection. Auto-initializes docs/acf/organization.md, audits compliance, and ensures everything stays in its proper place.

plugins.name: acf-whip
plugins.description: Hostile workflow enforcer. Zero tolerance backlog automation from decomposition to acceptance with aggressive quality gates. Workflow-native (2.0.0): /task and /go run as dynamic workflows whose loop, slug partition, dependency gate, and topological integration live in a deterministic script — Claude's context stays flat across iterations — with the legacy single-context loop as automatic fallback when dynamic workflows are unavailable. Slug enforcement in three layers: schema-required worktree slug at decomposition, a JS validation gate (kebab slugs, acyclic deps, unique ids), and a doctor FATAL at dispatch. Concurrency-safe: parallel across worktrees, sequential within a worktree. Autonomous integration: /go folds accepted worktrees into the local trunk each iteration with intelligent specialist-driven conflict resolution; dependency-gated dispatch ensures dependents only start from a codebase containing all integrated dependencies. Backlog state synchronizes at the repo root: task-engineer always operates at root, and the orchestrator owns all .backlog/ state moves on the trunk branch. Lock-file backoff: never removes .git/index.lock; sleeps and retries (1s→2s→4s) when contended. Worktree lifecycle extracted to tested shell scripts (clean-checkout, hydrate, integrate, apply-transition, scan-backlog) shared via skills/lib; /whip-doctor diagnoses backlog and worktree health; hydrate-worktree provisions ignored config (.env, node_modules) into fresh worktrees with secret-safety. Self-healing (2.0.1): the doctor derives and writes a missing worktree slug for active code tasks instead of hard-failing, and treats accepted/historical tasks as advisory (WARN, never blocking) — a pre-2.0.0 backlog runs to completion instead of aborting the gate. Branchless historical accepted tasks count as terminal and are never re-integrated (no phantom-fetch retry loop). Planning (decomposition) and execution (the /go loop) default to maximum parallelism: distinct worktree slug per independent surface, shared slug only on real file-surface overlap, and dependencies declared only on genuine output consumption. Scales to large lived-in backlogs (2.0.2): the per-iteration scan emits a bounded WORKING-SET snapshot — full objects only for actionable tasks plus any dependency targets, while terminal/historical accepted tasks collapse into aggregate runtime-terminal counts — so the workflow scheduler never has to echo a backlog-sized JSON blob through an agent (the prior cause of a multi-minute stall on a 300-task backlog). The doctor gains a --quiet mode that bounds report output to FATAL findings plus the grouped breakdown. Workflow state-machine parity (2.0.3): the /go workflow now performs the two transitions the migration had dropped — blocked→pending unblock when a task's dependencies resolve (gated on rejection-count so max-rejection redesign blocks stay for a human), and in-progress→blocked timeout at the operator threshold (ACFW_INPROGRESS_TIMEOUT_HOURS, default 8h, emitted by scan-backlog) — so a backlog whose pending tasks are gated on blocked tasks runs to completion instead of exiting no-progress. /task aborts before writing files when no specialist agents are installed (a backlog /go's bootstrap gate would otherwise reject). Retained dependency-target accepted tasks are emitted slim, and a one-shot re-scan absorbs a single garbled snapshot echo. The pure scheduling/terminal logic is extracted behind markers and unit-tested (tests/phase2-scheduler).

plugins.name: acf-nitro
plugins.description: Parallel execution enforcement mode - Enthusiastic speed demon who catches sequential execution violations and calculates time waste. Enforces TodoWrite batching, parallel Task spawning, and parallel tool calls.

plugins.name: acf-mission-control
plugins.description: Mission Control HUD for Claude Code - Track position, git branch, and context fuel with color-coded bar (green → yellow → red). Full situational awareness.

plugins.name: acf-advisor
plugins.description: Two skills for second opinions: `advisor` consults another LLM (thinking on by default) for one focused take; `board` convenes a multi-persona panel hypertailored to the decision, run as parallel advisor.py calls and synthesized by the orchestrator with weighting on the user-chosen priority dimension. Calls any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; comma-delimited ADVISOR_MODEL declares a multi-model pool for round-robin or cross-model triangulation. Per-family param-shape routing (Claude adaptive, Gemini thinking_level, OpenAI reasoning_effort) with ADVISOR_PROFILE override and shape-swap retry. Falls back to a local-team mode (Claude subagents roleplay personas) when no endpoint is configured.
